policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'Apphia our sister' (with the gloss note 'Greek the sister'), rendering the noun ἀδελφῇ, not the adjective ἀγαπητῇ ('beloved').
ASV renders both prepositions alike as 'toward'; πρὸς and εἰς are indistinguishable in the English, and the only note here is classed alternative_rendering.

The presence or absence of the article τοῦ before the following word leaves no trace in ASV 'unto Christ'; the verse's textual note concerns 'us' for 'you', a different word, and is not mapped to this unit.
ASV ends the verse 'unto Christ' with no 'Jesus', so it does not render the added Ἰησοῦν.
ASV 'I had much joy' renders χαρὰν ('joy'); Χάριν would give 'thanks'/'grace'.
ASV 'I had' is first person singular aorist, matching ἔσχον; ἔχομεν would be 'we have'.
ASV 'a prisoner also of Christ Jesus' follows the order Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, not Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
ASV 'in my bonds' is a natural rendering of the articular δεσμοῖς in a first-person clause and equally of δεσμοῖς μου; no note distinguishes the added pronoun.
ASV 'but now is profitable to thee and to me' has no correlative 'both', but an added intensive καὶ need not surface in English; nothing in the verse distinguishes the readings.
ASV has no imperative 'receive him', which excludes the RP reading σὺ δὲ αὐτόν … προσλαβοῦ; the remaining two readings carry the same wording and the English cannot separate them.
The variation is word order only (μοι διακονῇ / διακονῇ μοι); ASV 'he might minister unto me' renders either.
ἐλλόγα and ἐλλόγει are alternative imperative forms of the same verb; ASV 'put that to mine account' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'refresh my heart in Christ' renders Χριστῷ; κυρίῳ would repeat 'in the Lord' from the first clause.
ASV 'beyond what I say' is number-neutral in English and renders the plural ἃ or the singular ὃ alike.
ASV 'Epaphras … saluteth thee' is singular, matching Ἀσπάζεταί; the plural Ἀσπάζονταί would give 'salute'.
ASV reads 'our Lord Jesus Christ', rendering ἡμῶν; the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read the' marks the pronoun-less reading as the variant, not the text.
ASV prints 'Amen.' in the text with the mapped note 'Many ancient authorities omit Amen', so the ASV text carries Ἀμήν.
